Exhibit 99.1
News Release
The Coca-Cola Company Names David Elkins as Incoming Chief Financial Officer
Elkins to Succeed John Murphy, Who Will Continue to Serve as President of the Company
ATLANTA, Nov. 23, 2026 – The Coca-Cola Company today announced that David Elkins, a finance leader
with extensive experience across global pharmaceuticals and consumer products companies, will become executive vice president and chief
financial officer of Coca-Cola April 2, 2027, succeeding John Murphy.
Elkins has served as EVP and CFO of Bristol Myers Squibb since 2019, and
his past roles include positions with Johnson & Johnson and AstraZeneca.
Murphy, 64, intends to retire in 2027, with timing determined later to allow
for a smooth and orderly leadership transition for the CFO role. Murphy, who has been CFO since 2019, has been working with company leadership
for some time to prepare for the succession process.
Murphy will continue to serve as president, focusing on key enterprise priorities
in 2027, in addition to the CFO transition. As CFO, Elkins’ oversight will include finance, global strategy and Enterprise Services.
Elkins and Murphy will both report to CEO Henrique Braun.
“John has been a transformational leader during his 38 years at Coca-Cola,
especially through his most recent service as president and CFO,” Braun said. “I am very happy John will ensure a smooth transition
and provide valuable perspective as we maintain our focus on growing the company.”
“David comes to Coca-Cola with a track record of success across complex,
global companies,” Braun said. “He brings a strong understanding of finance and has developed future leaders. He will bring
complementary skills to our highly experienced leadership team.”
More About David Elkins
Elkins, 58, has been responsible for the Global Business Operations organization
at Bristol Myers Squibb, which consists of finance, business development, Global Financial Services & Operational Excellence, procurement
and investor relations.
Elkins joined the company in 2019 when it acquired Celgene, where he was
serving as EVP and CFO. He joined Celgene in 2018 after several years at Johnson & Johnson, where he was CFO for the consumer products
and medical device businesses and corporate functions.
Earlier, Elkins held roles with Becton, Dickinson, a leading global medical
device company, and pharmaceutical and biotechnology company AstraZeneca. He began his career in finance at The Boeing Co.
Elkins is a member of the board of directors of Tapestry Inc.
Elkins earned a bachelor’s degree in economics from the University
of Delaware, a master’s degree in organizational dynamics from the University of Pennsylvania and an MBA from Drexel University.
About John Murphy
Murphy was named CFO in 2019 and president in 2022. From 2016 to 2018, he
served as president of the company’s Asia Pacific group.
Murphy began his career with Coca-Cola in 1988 and went on to hold a variety
of general management, finance and strategic planning roles around the world.
For more about Murphy’s background, visit https://www.coca-colacompany.com/about-us/leadership/john-murphy.
About The Coca-Cola Company
The Coca-Cola Company (NYSE: KO) is a total beverage company with products
sold in more than 200 countries and territories. Our company’s purpose is to refresh the world and make a difference. We sell
multiple billion-dollar brands across several beverage categories worldwide. Our portfolio of sparkling soft drink brands includes
Coca-Cola, Sprite and Fanta. Our water, sports, coffee and tea brands include Dasani, smartwater, vitaminwater, Topo Chico, BODYARMOR,
Powerade, Costa, Georgia, Fuze Tea, Gold Peak and Ayataka. Our juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverage brands include Minute
Maid, Simply, innocent, Del Valle, fairlife and Santa Clara. We’re constantly transforming our portfolio, from reducing sugar in
our drinks to bringing innovative new products to market. We seek to positively impact people’s lives, communities and the planet
through water replenishment, packaging recycling, sustainable sourcing practices and carbon emissions reductions across our value chain.
Together with our bottling partners, we employ more than 700,000 people, helping bring economic opportunity to local communities worldwide.
Learn more at www.coca-colacompany.com and follow us on Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn.
Contacts:
Investors and Analysts: Todd Beiger, koinvestorrelations@coca-cola.com
Media: Scott Leith, sleith@coca-cola.com

Item
5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory
Arrangements of Certain Officers.
On November 23, 2026, The Coca-Cola Company (the “Company”)
announced that David V. Elkins will succeed John Murphy as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective April 2, 2027.
Mr. Murphy will continue to serve as President of the Company. Mr. Murphy intends to retire at a later date in 2027.
Mr. Elkins, age 58, has served as Executive Vice President
and Chief Financial Officer of Bristol Myers Squibb Company (“BMS”) since 2019. He joined BMS in connection with its acquisition
of Celgene Corporation, where he served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Before joining Celgene Corporation, Mr.
Elkins held senior finance positions at Johnson & Johnson. His prior experience also includes roles at Becton, Dickinson and Company
and AstraZeneca PLC. He began his career in finance at The Boeing Company.
In connection with Mr. Elkins’ appointment, the
Company provided Mr. Elkins a letter setting forth the primary compensation elements that will be effective upon the commencement of his
employment and the Company and Mr. Elkins separately entered into a deferred cash agreement providing for the replacement of certain compensation
he will forfeit from BMS.
Pursuant to Mr. Elkins’ letter, his base salary
will be $1,180,000. Mr. Elkins will be eligible to participate in the Company’s annual and long-term incentive programs, and his
target annual incentive will be 135% of his annual base salary.
Following the commencement of Mr. Elkins’ employment,
the Company will present to the Talent and Compensation Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors for approval one-time awards
intended to replace equity that Mr. Elkins will forfeit from BMS upon joining the Company, which one-time awards consist of (i) restricted
stock units with an approximate grant-date value of $5,400,000, expected to vest in two equal installments in February 2028 and February
2029, and (ii) deferred cash in the aggregate amount of $5,400,000, expected to be paid in two equal installments in February 2028 and
February 2029, in each case subject to continued employment through the vesting or payment dates, as applicable, as well as the other terms
and conditions of the applicable agreement.
Pursuant to the deferred cash agreement, Mr. Elkins
will also be eligible to receive a one-time cash payment in 2028, intended to replace the annual incentive he forfeits for the portion
of 2027 during which he was employed by BMS. The amount of the payment will be based on BMS’s 2027 performance and prorated for
the portion of 2027 during which Mr. Elkins was employed by BMS, subject to the terms and conditions of the deferred cash agreement.
The letter also provides that Mr. Elkins may receive
a one-time cash payment of $300,000 if he does not receive certain one-time contributions from BMS under its retirement and deferred compensation
programs. In addition, the letter provides for make-whole compensation if, as a result of his employment with the Company, Mr. Elkins
forfeits his 2026 annual incentive award or certain BMS equity scheduled to vest in March 2027.
Mr. Elkins will be subject to the Company’s share
ownership guidelines, and he will receive certain additional benefits described in his letter.
The foregoing descriptions of Mr. Elkins’ letter
and deferred cash agreement are qualified in their entirety by the terms of such letter and agreement, copies of which are attached hereto
as Exhibits 10.1 and 10.2, respectively, and incorporated herein by reference. Details regarding the Company’s annual and long-term
incentive programs are included in the Compensation Discussion and Analysis section of the Company’s definitive proxy statement
for the 2026 Annual Meeting of Shareowners filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on March 16, 2026.
There are no arrangements or understandings between
Mr. Elkins and any other person pursuant to which he was selected as an officer of the Company. Mr. Elkins does not have any family relationship
with any director or executive officer of the Company and is not a party to any transaction requiring disclosure under Item 404(a) of
Regulation S-K.
A copy of the Company’s press release announcing
these changes is furnished to this report as Exhibit 99.1.

NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director
SANTA CLARA, Calif.—November 23, 2026—NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer, and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.
"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA's Chief Financial Officer." Mr. Jones will continue to serve as Board chair.
“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry, and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”
As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.
The Board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The committee is engaging counsel with experience in national security matters, and such counsel will be retaining advisors with expertise in national security matters. NVIDIA is commencing a search to fill a new position,
Chief Compliance Officer, to oversee compliance across NVIDIA and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.
